newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot resids mostly hold despite crude rally.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot resids mostly hold despite crude rally.

text.p: U.S. spot fuel oil prices held relatively steady Monday in lackluster trade, with another sharp rally in crude partly offset by still-slack East Coast utility demand, industry sources said.

"The market doesn't feel soft with crude up again, and firm bunkers are still helping high sulphur, but we're looking for direction," said one trader, noting little actual utility demand though there has been talk of demand into Florida.
In New York Harbor, physical one percent was unchanged at about $15.25 a barrel, with May one percent paper also steady at $15.25-40 despite the crude run up, traders said.
With natgas prices showing signs of softening, traders said fading spring demand offered little hope for a significant rally near-term unless crude continued higher.
NYH 0.3 percent high pour was little changed from Friday at $16.25. High sulphurs in New York also held steady.
At the U.S. Gulf, prices were stable, with one percent still in the low-$15s and three percent at $13.50.
No NYH or USG deals were reported.

New York city gate swing gas prices slipped about a nickel Monday to the mid-$2.30s/mmBtu, or $14.87 a barrel equivalent. Gas at Henry Hub, the NYMEX delivery point, was down slightly to about $2.08/mmBtu, or $13.10 a barrel.
